item.title: Kanazawa Gold Leaf: 99% of Japan's Gold Leaf Production — Guide
item.description: Kanazawa produces roughly 99% of Japan’s gold leaf (kinpaku), a centuries-old craft tradition supported by the region’s naturally soft, mineral-rich water, ideal for the painstaking process of hammering gold into leaves thinner than a human hair. The craft’s influence is visible throughout the city, from gold leaf decoration on lacquerware and temple interiors to gold-flaked ice cream, sweets and cosmetics sold in shops across town, and hands-on workshops let visitors try applying gold leaf themselves to items like chopsticks, boxes or fans to take home.
